independent_solution: Air resistance acts opposite to the velocity, so it has a horizontal component that keeps reducing v_x (no longer constant) and a vertical component that adds to gravity on the way up and opposes it on the way down.
Mechanical energy is lost throughout, so the maximum height and range are smaller than the vacuum parabola's, and the particle comes down more slowly horizontally than it went up.
Hence the path is not a parabola: an asymmetric curve with the apex shifted towards the landing point and a descending branch steeper than the ascending one.
questions.independent_answer: Lower, shorter, asymmetric curve whose fall is steeper than its rise, because energy and the horizontal velocity keep decreasing.
questions.official_answer: Due to air resistance, particle energy as well as horizontal component of velocity keep on decreasing making the fall steeper than rise

independent_solution: Options read on the pinned page. Molecules hit the leading face with relative speed about u + v and the trailing face with about u - v; momentum flux goes as the square of the relative speed, so the pressure difference is proportional to (u+v)^2 - (u-v)^2 = 4uv: [A] true.
Resistive force = pressure difference x area, proportional to v: [B] true.
Then m dv/dt = F - k v: the acceleration decreases as v grows, so [C] is false; v approaches the terminal value F/k, where F balances the resistive force: [D] true. Answer A, B, D.
Full question read on pinned page 20. Mass of the drop (water, 1000 kg/m^3): m = 1000 x (4/3) pi (2e-3)^3 = 3.35e-5 kg.
Work by gravity in each 250 m half: m g h = 3.35e-5 x 9.8 x 250 = 0.082 J (same in both halves; it does not depend on the drag).
Work-energy over the whole fall from rest: W_g + W_r = (1/2) m v^2 = 0.5 x 3.35e-5 x 100 = 1.68e-3 J, so W_r = 1.68e-3 - 0.164 = -0.163 J.
questions.independent_answer: 0.082 J by gravity in each half; -0.163 J by the resistive force
